iron1: RDJ improvised large parts of his dialogue — including the final 'I am Iron Man', which established the MCU's post-credit standard.
Marvel financed the film itself and mortgaged the film rights to its characters to do it — had it flopped, there would be no MCU.
av1: The Battle of New York is the time-travel destination in Endgame — and the moment Loki's Tesseract escape triggers the entire Loki series.
The shawarma meal after the credits was shot one day after the premiere.
cap2: The film with which the Russo brothers (previously: sitcom directors!) earned the trust for Infinity War, Endgame and now Doomsday.
cw: The airport duel was built almost entirely digitally — Spider-Man's MCU debut was kept secret until the premiere.
iw: Thanos has more screen time than any Avenger — the Russos call him the actual protagonist.
The Snap cliffhanger stayed unresolved for a year; 'Mr. Stark, I don't feel so good' became a meme instantly.
eg: At $2.799 billion, for a time the most successful film of all time.
'I am Iron Man' as the last line was a late reshoot idea — in the script, Tony initially died without a word.
nwh: Maguire and Garfield were denied right up to the premiere — despite leaked set photos.
Second most successful Spider-Man film of all time ($1.9 billion).
mom: Sam Raimi returned 20 years after his Spider-Man trilogy — complete with a Bruce Campbell cameo and his horror signature.
l1: The TVA aesthetic is based on 70s bureaucracy design; Miss Minutes was voiced live on set by an actress.
Kang's casting as He Who Remains was the original cornerstone of the whole saga — until the Doom pivot came.
l2: The finale 'Glorious Purpose' is considered one of the best MCU episodes ever — Loki's sacrifice ends his 14-year arc from villain to god.
dw: Most successful R-rated film of all time ($1.34 billion).
Over 20 cameos, from the Blade comeback to Chris Evans as Johnny Storm — not as Steve Rogers.
tb: The asterisk in the title was only resolved after release: 'The New Avengers'.
Sentry's Void sequences were co-developed by Beau DeMayo and are considered the boldest depiction of depression in the MCU.
f4: Set entirely on Earth-828 — named after Jack Kirby's birthday (August 28).
After the cloud debacle of 2007, Galactus was shown fully physical for the first time (Ralph Ineson).
qm: Jonathan Majors' conviction a few months after release led to the biggest course correction in MCU history: Kang Dynasty became Doomsday.
wv: Every episode imitates a different sitcom decade — including real live-audience laughter recordings for the 50s episodes.
bnd: First Spider-Man solo film directed by Destin Daniel Cretton (Shang-Chi) — and the last Marvel theatrical film before Doomsday.
doomsday: RDJ's Doom reveal at SDCC 2024 ('New mask, same task') is already considered one of the biggest casting coups in cinema history.
The chairs livestream for the cast announcement ran over 5 hours and broke Marvel's viewing records.
x97: Direct continuation of the 90s series — the Genosha episode 'Remember It' is considered one of the best Marvel episodes ever.
xmen1: Hugh Jackman was a last-minute replacement for Dougray Scott (stuck on Mission: Impossible 2) — the role of his life.
x3: Kelsey Grammer's Beast returns 17 years later in The Marvels' post-credit scene — and now in Doomsday.
dofp: Essentially Fox's Endgame: connects both cast generations and erases the events of X3 from the timeline.
logan: First superhero film with an Oscar nomination for adapted screenplay.
Johnny Cash's 'Hurt' in the trailer defined an entire trailer era.
dp1: The leaked 2014 test footage (allegedly planted by insiders) forced Fox into a greenlight after 11 years of development hell.
f405: Chris Evans played Johnny Storm — 6 years before becoming Captain America. His mysterious Doomsday casting might close the circle right here.
raimi2: Won the Oscar for visual effects; the operating-room scene with Doc Ock's arms is pure Raimi horror heritage.
raimi3: Sony forced Venom in against Raimi's will — the planned fourth film died, and Raimi's trilogy with it.
tasm2: Gwen Stacy's death ended Sony's Sinister Six plans; the rights panic that followed led directly to the MCU deal for Spider-Man.
venom1: Despite 30% on Rotten Tomatoes: $856 million — the audience/critic divide as a business model.
venom2: The post-credit scene teleports Eddie into the MCU (No Way Home era) — to this day the most direct Sony-Marvel bridge.
morbius: Flopped, became a meme ('It's Morbin' Time'), was re-released because of the memes — and flopped a second time. Unique in cinema history.
madameweb: The trailer monologue about the Amazon became the meme of the year — and isn't even in the finished film.
kraven: Sony announced the film as the studio's first R-rated Marvel — it became the very last film of the SSU.
sv1: Oscar for best animated film — the comic-punk look changed the entire animation industry (see Puss in Boots, Mutant Mayhem).
sv2: Over 1,000 animators worked on six different animation styles — every dimension has its own look.
thor1: Kenneth Branagh staged Asgard as Shakespearean drama — hence all the Dutch angles.
Hawkeye's MCU debut: Renner hangs unnoticed in the crane.
cap1: Skinny Steve was created with digital tricks and a body double — Evans shot every scene twice.
gotg1: Hollywood considered a talking raccoon career suicide — $773 million later, James Gunn was a genius.
av2: The comic 'Age of Ultron' has nothing to do with the film — Marvel just liked the title.
antman1: Edgar Wright worked on the film for eight years and left shortly before shooting — remnants of his script are still in it.
strange1: Casting Tilda Swinton as the Ancient One sparked a whitewashing debate that Marvel later publicly called a mistake.
spider1: 'Homecoming' means the school dance AND the character's return to Marvel — the Sony deal was born from the panic after Amazing Spider-Man 2.
thor3: According to Waititi, around 80% of the dialogue is improvised — and Korg is Waititi himself.
bp1: First superhero film with Oscar wins (costume, production design, score) and a Best Picture nomination.
antman2: First MCU film with a heroine in the title — three years before Captain Marvel.
cm: Samuel L. Jackson was digitally de-aged by 25 years for the entire film — a first at the time.
Goose isn't a cat but a Flerken. That explains the Tesseract in the stomach.
spider2: Officially the closing film of the Infinity Saga — not Endgame.
bw: Came two years after the character's death — and led to Scarlett Johansson's lawsuit against Disney over the parallel streaming release.
sc: The bus fight is an open bow to Jackie Chan — choreographer Brad Allan was Chan's student.
et: Chloé Zhao's first film after her Nomadland Oscar — and the first MCU film with a love scene.
Harry Styles as Eros and Blade's voice in the credits: two threads that were never spun further.
hk: Visibly based on the celebrated Fraction/Aja comic run — including the Tracksuit Mafia and 'Bro'.
The Rogers musical later got a real production at Disneyland.
bpwf: Coogler rewrote the entire script after Chadwick Boseman's death — around the grief itself.
Riri Williams' debut, two years before her own series.
g3: Contains the first clearly spoken F-word in MCU history — the honor goes to Quill.
tlt: The screaming goats Toothgnasher and Toothgrinder are based on a Taylor Swift meme sound.
msm: 98% on Rotten Tomatoes — best critics' score of any MCU series, yet review-bombed on IMDb.
mk: Oscar Isaac's Steven Grant accent split the internet for days — he deliberately chose it 'too silly'.
shk: Officially brought Charlie Cox's Daredevil back into the MCU — in workshop-casual look.
si: At ~$212 million one of the most expensive series ever — and at 53% the weakest MCU reviews. The costliest lesson of the Marvel TV era.
ec: First series under the 'Marvel Spotlight' banner: deliberately watchable without multiverse homework — and the first TV-MA rating.
dba: Was completely rebuilt creatively mid-production — the original, more procedural version already existed half-shot.
wm: Trevor Slattery returns — Ben Kingsley's fourth Marvel appearance as the fake Mandarin.
vq: Terry Matalas (Picard S3) took over the series — James Spader's Ultron return was the casting coup of the year.
iron2: Made at breakneck speed because Marvel had to follow up Iron Man immediately — Favreau later openly called the pressure a problem.
iron3: The Mandarin twist split fans so badly that Marvel officially walked it back with the short film 'Hail to the King' — which became canon in Shang-Chi.
hulk: The forgotten MCU film: Edward Norton secretly co-wrote the script and was replaced by Mark Ruffalo afterwards.
The Leader was set up here in 2008 — the payoff came only in 2025.
thor2: Internally considered the low point of Phase 2 — director Alan Taylor complained about massive studio cuts.
Loki's fake death number two of three.
gotg2: Kurt Russell was fully digitally de-aged for the opening — and the Baby Groot dance is based on James Gunn's own dance video.
wbn: Shot entirely in black and white as an homage to Universal horror — composer Michael Giacchino directed for the first time.
ghs: James Gunn declared the special the 'favorite project of his career' — Kevin Bacon plays himself, because Footloose is world literature in GotG canon.
eow: Every episode is set in a different era of Wakandan history — animation as anthology.
x2: The opening — Nightcrawler's attack in the White House — is still considered one of the genre's best action scenes.
firstclass: Matthew Vaughn shot the film in just 13 months from signing to release — a record for a blockbuster this size.
wolv13: Based on the legendary 1982 Claremont/Miller Japan run — the director's cut is notably bloodier and better.
apoc: Oscar Isaac later openly called the shoot 'excruciating' — four hours of makeup daily, under which nobody recognized him.
darkphoenix: The finale was completely reshot because the original was too similar to Captain Marvel — the Fox-Disney deal ran parallel to production.
newmutants: Postponed three times over two years, inherited from Fox, buried by Disney without marketing — the announced reshoots never happened.
f407: Showing Galactus as a cloud is still considered a cardinal sin — First Steps (2025) demonstratively did the opposite.

iron1: Nick Fury waits in Tony's mansion: 'You've become part of a bigger universe' — the Avenger Initiative is born. THE scene that invented the post-credits concept.
hulk: Tony Stark joins General Ross at the bar — the MCU's first cross-film connection.
iron2: Agent Coulson reports a find in New Mexico: Mjölnir in the crater.
thor1: Selvig meets Fury — and Loki lurks in his reflection. The Tesseract enters the stage.
cap1: Steve wakes up in the present; Fury has a mission — straight into the first Avengers teaser.
av1: The Other warns his master — Thanos turns around, grinning. Six years of build-up start here.
The exhausted Avengers eat shawarma in silence. Shot one day after the world premiere.
iron3: Tony tells the whole story to Bruce Banner — who is unsuited as a therapist: 'I'm not that kind of doctor.'
thor2: Sif and Volstagg hand the Aether to the Collector: 'One down, five to go.'
Thor returns to Jane; a frost beast chases London pigeons.
cap2: Baron von Strucker experiments with Loki's scepter — in the cells: 'the twins', Wanda and Pietro.
Bucky stands in the Smithsonian in front of his own memorial plaque.
gotg1: Baby Groot dances to 'I Want You Back' — as long as Drax isn't looking.
The Collector sits in the rubble — next to Howard the Duck.
av2: Thanos reaches for the gauntlet himself: 'Fine, I'll do it myself.'
antman1: Hank shows Hope the Wasp prototype: 'It's about time.'
Sam and Steve have found Bucky — 'I know a guy.'
cw: Bucky has himself frozen in Wakanda; T'Challa grants asylum.
Peter discovers the Spider-Signal in his new web-shooter.
strange1: Strange counsels Thor over self-refilling beer: 'So — Loki.'
Mordo takes Pangborn's magic: 'Too many sorcerers.'
gotg2: Five scenes at once — the most important: Ayesha's secret project in the birthing pod is called 'Adam'. Adam Warlock is coming.
Teenage Groot won't clean up; Stakar reassembles the old Ravagers.
spider1: Vulture protects Peter's identity in prison — honor among neighbors.
Captain America lectures on patience: 'Sometimes you wait… for nothing.' A meta gag about the wait itself.
thor3: A gigantic ship slides in front of the Asgardian ark: Sanctuary II. Thanos has arrived.
The Grandmaster congratulates his revolutionaries on a draw.
bp1: T'Challa opens Wakanda before the UN: 'We will share.'
Bucky wakes up healed in Wakanda — the children call him 'White Wolf'.
iw: Fury crumbles to dust — his last reach is for a retro pager with a star logo.
antman2: Scott collects quantum particles — then Hank, Hope and Janet crumble to dust. The Snap at point-blank range.
The giant ant calmly plays the drums.
cm: The pager goes silent — Carol suddenly stands in Avengers HQ: 'Where's Fury?'
Goose retches up the Tesseract onto Fury's desk.
spider2: J. Jonah Jameson (original Simmons!) reveals Mysterio's doctored video — and Peter's identity. Worldwide.
'Fury' was Talos the whole time — the real one is on vacation on a Skrull spaceship.
bw: Yelena at her sister's grave — Valentina gives her a target: the man 'responsible for it'. A photo of Clint.
sc: Wong, Carol and Bruce are puzzled: the Ten Rings are broadcasting a signal — to whom? Unanswered to this day.
Xialing takes over the Ten Rings organization, contrary to her announcement.
et: Eros — Thanos' brother, played by Harry Styles — offers the Eternals help. Since then: radio silence.
Dane Whitman hesitates before the Ebony Blade, a voice asks: 'Sure you're ready for that, Mr. Whitman?' — it's Blade.
nwh: Eddie Brock vanishes back into his universe — a drop of symbiote stays behind on the counter. It's still out there.
The complete first MoM trailer as a 'scene' — Strange's chaos begins.
mom: Clea (Charlize Theron) cuts a portal into reality: 'You caused an incursion, and we're going to fix it.' Strange follows her — open thread number one.
Pizza Poppa finally stops hitting himself: 'It's over!'
tlt: Zeus dispatches his son: Hercules — played by Brett Goldstein. Not seen since.
Jane reaches Valhalla, greeted by Heimdall.
bpwf: Shuri meets Nakia's son: Toussaint — T'Challa's child, Prince of Wakanda. The future of the Panther line.
qm: An arena full of Kang variants: the Council of Kangs convenes — Rama-Tut, Immortus, Scarlet Centurion. Never picked up again.
Victor Timely presents his inventions in 1901 — in the audience: an alarmed Loki and Mobius.
g3: The new Guardians around Captain Rocket, Adam Warlock and Phyla — Groot's first audible sentence.
Legendary Star-Lord: Quill has breakfast with his grandfather. Title card: 'Star-Lord will return.'
mv: Kamala recruits Kate Bishop for a team — the Young Avengers begin here.
Monica wakes up in a foreign universe — next to her 'mother' and a very blue Dr. Hank McCoy: Beast. Welcome to the X-Men.
dw: Deadpool 'proves' Johnny Storm's innocence with archive footage — immortalizing Chris Evans' cursing tirade.
bnw: The Leader warns Sam from his cell: 'The others are coming' — other worlds.
tb: The New Avengers in everyday life — including a naming dispute with Sam's lawyers.
14 months later: a ship with a '4' on the hull reaches Earth-616. The Fantastic Four are here.
f4: Four years later: Sue doesn't find Franklin alone — a figure in a green cloak and metal mask kneels before him. Doom has found him. The first scene of the Doomsday run-up.
An animated credits sequence in 60s style — centerpiece: the F4 as a cartoon.
wv: Monica learns from a Skrull: 'An old friend of your mother's' wants to see her — up there.
Wanda studies the Darkhold as an astral projection — and hears her sons calling.
fws: Sharon Carter, pardoned, on the phone: the Power Broker is back in business — with government access.
msm: Kamala's bangle pulls her away — and Captain Marvel stands confused in her room. Direct transition into The Marvels.
mk: A third personality: Jake Lockley chauffeurs Harrow away on Khonshu's orders.
ag: Agatha's ghost accompanies Billy — outside waits the search for Tommy: the second twin.
ih: Riri has signed: Mephisto smiles, her grief is gone — the price still open.
hk: No twist, no teaser — instead the complete musical number 'Save The City' from Rogers: The Musical in full length. Marvel's cheekiest credits.
x3: Moira MacTaggert's comatose patient speaks with Xavier's voice: 'Hello, Moira.' He lives.
origins: Weapon XI alias 'Deadpool' — the sewn-shut Wade reaches for his head. Ryan Reynolds got his revenge seven years later.
wolv13: Two years later at the airport: Magneto AND Professor X recruit Logan — a threat approaches.
dofp: Egypt, millennia earlier: a crowd worships En Sabah Nur, who builds pyramids with his mind. Four horsemen on the horizon.
apoc: Men from Essex Corp secure Wolverine's blood samples — the name behind X-23 and Mister Sinister.
dp1: Deadpool in the Ferris Bueller bathrobe: 'Go home!' — and announces Cable.
dp2: Deadpool uses Cable's time device to 'fix' the timeline — including executing the Origins Deadpool and the Green Lantern script.
tasm1: A man in the shadows asks Connors in his cell: 'Did you tell the boy the truth about his father?' Never resolved.
venom1: Eddie interviews a red-haired inmate in San Quentin: Cletus Kasady promises 'carnage'.
Plus: a complete Spider-Verse preview scene — Sony advertising its own animated film.
venom2: A flash of light — and Eddie suddenly sits in a strange hotel room, on TV: J. Jonah Jameson about Peter Parker. Venom is in the MCU.
venom3: In the dark of the symbiote homeworld, Knull opens his eyes: 'My deathbringer will come.' A tease without a planned film.
morbius: Vulture materializes — through the NWH spell?? — in Morbius' universe and proposes founding a team. Makes no sense to this day and remains Marvel's most confusing credits scene.
sv1: Miguel O'Hara — Spider-Man 2099 — tests the dimension jump and lands in the 60s cartoon series of all places: the double-pointing meme, official.

pcNotes.eg: No scene — the only major MCU film without one. Instead: the hammering of Tony's first armor as an audio farewell.
pcNotes.logan: No scene. Mangold insisted: after this ending, nobody gets to laugh.
pcNotes.tasm2: Curious: an X-Men DoFP scene ran mid-credits — the result of a Fox/Sony contract deal, no story connection.
pcNotes.madameweb: No post-credit scene — the franchise was over faster than the credits.
pcNotes.sv2: No credits bonus — the film itself IS the cliffhanger. 'Beyond the Spider-Verse' is still pending.

cameo.iron1: Mistaken for Hugh Hefner by Tony — bathrobe blondes included.
cameo.hulk: Drinks the soda with Banner's gamma blood — and keels over.
cameo.iron2: This time the Larry King mix-up, suspenders included.
cameo.thor1: Tries to pull Mjölnir out of the crater with his pickup. The truck bed loses.
cameo.cap1: General at the medal ceremony: 'I thought he'd be taller.'
cameo.av1: In a TV interview: 'Superheroes in New York? Give me a break!'
cameo.iron3: Beauty pageant judge, holds up a 10.
cameo.thor2: Psychiatric patient: 'Can I have my shoe back now?'
cameo.cap2: Smithsonian guard in front of the empty Cap display: 'Oh, I am SO fired.'
cameo.av2: Veteran at Thor's party; the Asgardian liquor wins.
cameo.cw: FedEx courier at the end: 'Are you Tony Stank?'
cameo.strange1: Reads Aldous Huxley on the bus, laughing.
cameo.gotg2: Tells the Watchers about his jobs — the official confirmation of the fan theory: all cameos are ONE character.
cameo.spider1: Neighbor Gary, yelling from the window: 'Don't make me come down there!'
cameo.thor3: The barber of Sakaar — cuts Thor's hair with a trembling multi-blade thing.
cameo.iw: Bus driver during the invasion: 'What's the matter? You never seen a spaceship before?'
cameo.antman2: His car shrinks: 'The sixties were great, but now I'm paying for it.'
cameo.cm: Reads his own Mallrats script on the train — the first posthumous cameo, with the 'Thank you, Stan' logo.
cameo.eg: 1970, in the car with a hippie beard: 'Make love, not war!' — his final MCU appearance.
cameo.raimi1: Saves a girl from falling debris — his first big Marvel movie cameo.
cameo.raimi2: Pulls someone out of the danger zone again. Routine.
cameo.raimi3: Tells Peter: 'One person CAN make a difference.' — ''Nuff said.'
cameo.tasm1: Librarian with headphones while the school gets demolished behind him — fan favorite.
cameo.tasm2: Guest at Peter's graduation: 'I think I know that guy!'
cameo.xmen1: Hot dog vendor on the beach as Senator Kelly crawls out of the sea.
cameo.x3: Neighbor with a garden hose whose water refuses to fall, courtesy of Jean.
cameo.dp1: DJ in the strip club. It's the Deadpool universe.
cameo.venom1: Passer-by with a dog: 'Don't give up on her — either of you.' (posthumous)
cameo.sv1: Comic shop clerk about the suit: 'It always fits — eventually.' The most moving of them all (posthumous).

variants.note: One fate, infinite lives — with great power comes the same thing in every universe.
The same person, two fates: he became the God of Stories, she killed one.
2005 Johnny Storm, 2011 Captain America — and the Doomsday role is secret. The circle might close.
Tony Stark is dead. Doctor Doom wears his face. Marvel swears it's a coincidence. Nobody believes Marvel.
